Game Theory in Modern Economics: A Survey

This survey examines the application of game theory to contemporary economic problems, covering Nash equilibria, mechanism design, and auction theory.

Game theory has become an indispensable tool in modern economics. Since the foundational work of von Neumann and Morgenstern, and later Nash, game-theoretic models have been applied to understand strategic interactions in markets, political systems, and social institutions.

In this paper, we review three main areas: first, the development of Nash equilibrium concepts and their refinements; second, mechanism design theory and its applications to market design; and third, auction theory and its practical applications in spectrum auctions and online advertising.

Our analysis suggests that while game theory has provided powerful insights, its predictive power depends heavily on assumptions about rationality and information that may not hold in practice.
